title: Purification and Application of Genetically Encoded Potassium Ion Indicators for Quantification of Potassium Ion Concentrations within Biological Samples
protocol: Transform the plasmid encoding GEPII 1.0 into chemically competent BL21(DE3) E. coli cells.
Plate the transformed cells on LB medium with 50 µg/ml kanamycin sulfate and incubate overnight at 37°C.
Pick a single colony from the plate and inoculate it in LB medium containing 50 µg/ml kanamycin sulfate, then grow overnight at 37°C with shaking.
Inoculate 1 liter of LB medium with 50 µg/ml kanamycin sulfate using an overnight culture and incubate until OD600 reaches approximately 0.6-0.8.
Induce expression by adding IPTG to a final concentration of 0.4 mM, then continue incubation at 37°C for an additional 2 hours.
Harvest the cells by centrifugation at 4°C and resuspend in lysis buffer supplemented with Benzonase nuclease and bacterial protease inhibitor cocktail.
Lyse the cells using sonication or a French press, then clear the lysate by centrifugation to remove debris.
Apply the cleared lysate to an affinity column equilibrated with storage buffer.
Wash the column with Wash Buffer 1 until no protein is detected in the flowthrough.
Elute the bound GEPII 1.0 using elution buffer (not specified, assume appropriate for affinity method).
Collect and pool eluted fractions containing pure GEPII 1.0.
Concentrate and dialyze the purified GEPII 1.0 as necessary to obtain a final concentration of 3-5 mg/ml in storage buffer.
Store aliquots at -80°C until use for quantification of [K+] in various biological samples.
Let E. coli BL21(DE3) cells thaw on ice and aliquot 50 µl into a 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tube.
Quickly re-freeze the tube containing the bacterial stock at −80°C.
Add 50-100 ng plasmid DNA encoding GEPII 1.0 to the 50 µl of bacteria.
Mix by carefully moving the pipette tip.
Incubate on ice for 30 min.
Heat shock the cells at 42°C for 10 s.
Incubate in ice for 5 min.
Add 950 µl SOC medium and incubate at 37°C for 1 h with shaking.
Add 10 ml LB medium containing 50 µg/µl kanamycin sulfate to 15-ml conical tubes.
Inoculate with bacterial culture and cultivate overnight at 37°C.
Pipet 350 µl of 50% glycerol solution into sterile 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tubes.
Add 500 µl bacterial culture to the glycerol solution.
Immediately freeze glycerol stocks at −80°C.
Induce protein expression
Inoculate 1 L LB medium (with kanamycin) with transformed bacterial culture and incubate with shaking at 37°C until the OD600 reaches 0.6-0.8 (typically, 4-6 hr).
Add 1 mM IPTG to induced protein expression and incubate for 4-6 hr at 20°C with shaking.
Transfer bacterial suspension to centrifuge tubes and pellet cells at 7,800 × g (6,000 rpm in Sorvall LYNX Superspeed centrifuge) for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and resuspend pelleted cells in 15 ml lysis buffer.
Add 250 U Benzonase nuclease and 150 µl bacterial protease inhibitor cocktail (1:100 dilution) to the cell suspension and incubate on ice for 30 min.
Break up cells by sonicating for 20 min on ice, performing 10 s of sonication followed by 10 s of pause over a period of 20 min.
Centrifuge at 17,200 × g (10,000 rpm in Sorvall LYNX) for 45 min at 4°C to pellet cell debris.
Transfer supernatant to 15-ml conical tubes and keep on ice.
If desired, freeze centrifuged supernatant at −80°C.
Thaw frozen supernatant in a 37°C water bath before use.
Load an Econo-Pac Chromatography column with 3 ml pre-charged Protino Ni-NTA agarose.
Equilibrate column by filling to the top with lysis buffer (15 ml) and letting the buffer flow through.
Apply cell lysate to the column by carefully decanting or pipetting it.
Allow the lysate to flow through the column.
Wash column once each with 15 ml wash buffer 1 and then 15 ml wash buffer 2.
Elute protein with 15 ml of high-salt purification buffer.
If desired, freeze the protein solution in liquid nitrogen.
Thaw frozen eluate quickly in a 37°C water bath before use.
Concentrate the protein solution using Vivaspin concentrator tubes according to manufacturer's instructions.
Centrifuge at 2,300 × g (4,000 rpm in Eppendorf centrifuge) for 20 min at 4°C.
Repeat centrifugation until a volume of 500 µl protein remains in the collector.
Discard the flowthrough after each centrifugation if there is too much liquid at the bottom of the tube.
Insert a Superdex 200 increase 10/300 GL column into the Äkta pure system according to manufacturer's instructions.
Choose the “inlet” and “column position” and define the “system flow” in the Äkta pure system.
Set the column position at “Bypass” to avoid applying any impurities onto the column during washing.
Wash the selected pump system with SEC buffer.
Under “monitors”, select “wavelengths” to define the wavelengths that are shown on the screen.
Set wavelength to 480 nm to screen for the yellow fluorescent GEPII 1.0 protein.
Set alarms according to the used column.
Define the pre-column pressure and the delta column pressure.
Press “execute” to wash the system without the column.
Select the “manual load” option on the injection loop.
Apply 5 ml SEC buffer with a syringe onto the loop.
Switch from “manual load” to “inject” to wash the loop.
Change back to “manual load” on the loop and then remove the syringe.
Change from the “bypass” position to the actual column position.
Allow 30 ml SEC buffer to flow through the column to wash and equilibrate it.
With “manual load” selected in the software, use a small syringe to load protein solution from the concentrator tubes onto the loop.
Be careful to avoid any air bubbles.
Change to “inject” to apply the protein onto the column.
After ∼6 ml, start the fractionation to collect fractions containing protein.
Combine fractions containing protein.
Determine the protein concentration using a method of choice.
Calculate the molarity of the protein solution.
Dilute GEPII 1.0 in dilution buffer to a concentration of 400 nM.
Pipette 40 μl of the diluted GEPII into 14 wells of a black 96-well plate.
Add 40 μl of K+ calibration solutions (60 µM, 200 µM, 600 µM, 2 mM, 6 mM, and 20 mM) to duplicate wells.
Add 40 μl dilution buffer to the last two wells as a blank.

Measure all wells using the CLARIOstar Plus fluorescence plate reader with excitation at 430-20 nm, emission at 475-10 nm and 525-10 nm, dichroic filters at 455 nm and 480 nm, and gain set to 2,000 for both emissions.
Calculate FRET ratio values by determining the FRET/CFP fluorescence (525 nm/475 nm) for all wells.
Determine the average FRET ratio value from the blank wells.
Subtract the average blank value from each well containing K+ calibration solutions to obtain ΔRatio values.
Plot ΔRatio values against [K+] linearly and logarithmically.
Determine the EC50 from the plot.
Reconstitute recombinant purified GEPII 1.0.
Plot blank-corrected FRET ratio signals of GEPII 1.0 against [K+] linearly and logarithmically.
Determine the EC50 of GEPII 1.0 using sigmoidal concentration-response curve fitting.
Prepare aliquots as desired after proving functional.
Shock-freeze prepared aliquots in liquid nitrogen.
Store frozen aliquots up to 2 years at -80°C in darkness.
Repeat functionality tests if protein has been stored for more than one year before use.
Collect murine blood by phlebotomy from v. facialis.
Prepare murine serum samples after collecting blood.
Generate a K+ calibration curve for GEPII 1.0.
Determine [K+] in murine serum samples using GEPII 1.0.
Remove mouse from its environment and restrain it securely by grasping the neck scruff with the thumb and index finger and holding the base of the tail between the palm and the ring finger.
Puncture the superficial temporal vein using a sterile single-use lancet.
Collect blood from the second drop (∼20-30 μl) into a 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tube.
Lightly press the puncture site with a sterile gauze for a few seconds to cause hemostasis.
Release mouse from restraint and return it to its home cage.
Allow blood samples to clot for 15 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge samples for 10 min at 400 × g to separate the blood clot from the serum.
Carefully transfer serum to a new 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tube, taking care not to disturb the pelleted blood clot.
Place serum on ice.
Start over with a fresh blood sample if the blood clot is mixed with the serum.
Visually check sera for hemolysis.
Exclude samples and start over with fresh blood samples if hemolysis is visible.
Store serum samples at −20°C for up to 1 year or maintain on ice for direct analysis.
Pipette 40 µl of serum assay solution into each well needed for the calibration curve, using triplicate wells for each concentration.
Add 40 µl of each K+ calibration solution (200 µM, 300 µM, 400 µM, 500 µM, 600 µM, and 700 µM) to triplicate wells containing 40 µl serum assay solution.
Use 40 µl dilution buffer for blank wells.
Be very careful with pipetting when adding K+ to the wells.
Avoid air bubbles in pipetting during K+ addition.
Destroy any air bubbles using sterile needles if present.
Measure samples using a CLARIOstar Plus fluorescence plate reader without the lid on.
Set excitation to 430-20 nm for fluorescence measurements.
Set emission to 475-10 and 525-10 nm for fluorescence measurements.
Use dichroic filters at 455 and 480 nm during measurement.
Adjust gain settings to 2,000 for both emissions with focal height adjusted to blank.
Calculate the FRET ratio by determining the FRET/CFP fluorescence (525 nm/475 nm) of each well containing K+ calibration solution.
Calculate the FRET/CFP ratios of the blank wells.
Determine the average value of the blank well ratios.
Subtract that average from each value of the calibration curve.
Plot the blank-corrected FRET/CFP ratios (ΔRatio) against [K+].
Fit the values using a one-phase decay.
Create the equation of the curve and solve it for x.
Use the formula to calculate the [K+] from the FRET/CFP ratio of GEPII 1.0.
If serum samples were frozen, thaw them on ice.
Dilute 8 µl of each serum sample with 92 µl dilution buffer (1:12.5 dilution).
Mix by inverting tubes.
Do NOT vortex to avoid foaming.
Pipette 40 μl serum assay solution into duplicate wells of a 96-well plate for each K+ determination.
Include duplicate wells for the blank and both K+ standards.
Add 40 μl of each diluted sample and standard to the wells containing serum assay solution.
Use dilution buffer for the blank wells.
Avoid air bubbles during pipetting.
Destroy any air bubbles using sterile needles if present.
Measure fluorescence as previously indicated in step 11.
Calculate the FRET ratio by determining the FRET/CFP fluorescence (525 nm/475 nm) for each well.
Determine the average for the blank wells.
Subtract the blank well average from each sample and standard.
Verify the accuracy of the internal standards by calculating [K+] in mM using the formula generated from the calibration curve.
If K+ standard values deviate strongly, check several parameters as indicated in Critical Parameters and Troubleshooting.
Calculate the [K+] for the samples if standards are within range.
Determine the average of the duplicates for each sample.
Cultivate cells of interest to a confluency of ∼80% using appropriate culture medium and a humidified incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Wash INS-1 832/13 cells with PBS one day before the experiment.
Trypsinize cells using ∼3 ml trypsin solution for 2-4 min in a humidified 37°C incubator.
Suspend floating cells in 10 ml of medium to stop trypsinization.
Transfer cell suspension to a 30-ml multipurpose container and centrifuge at 200 × g for 10 min.
Remove the supernatant and wash cells with 10 ml PBS, then centrifuge again at 200 × g for 10 min.
Remove PBS and resuspend cell pellet in 10 ml of supplemented RPMI 1640 on ice.
Determine cell density using a Bürker-Türk counting chamber or another method.
Adjust cell suspension to approximately 250,000 cells/ml.
Seed 200 µl of the cell suspension (∼50,000 cells) in each well of black 96-well plates with clear bottoms.
Include at least two wells per condition containing 200 µl medium without cells for blank measurements.
Culture cells overnight and check cell density once cells reach 70%-80% confluence.
Wash wells twice with 250 µl of cell wash buffer.
Remove the cell wash buffer from all wells and replace it with 80 µl of cell assay solution containing either the compound of interest or vehicle.
Use at least two blank wells per condition for measurements.
Measure CFP and FRET signals of GEPII 1.0 over time using a CLARIOstar Plus fluorescence plate reader.
Set excitation to 430-20 nm, emissions to 475-10 nm and 525-10 nm, and dichroic filters to 455 nm and 480 nm.
Adjust gain settings to 2,000 for both emissions with focal height adjusted to blank wells.
Use bottom optics for measurements to prevent evaporation.
Add 5 µl of 850 µM digitonin stock solution to all wells including blanks (final 50 µM).
Calculate the FRET ratio signal of GEPII 1.0 by determining the FRET/CFP fluorescence (525 nm/475 nm) for all wells including blanks.
Perform blank correction of FRET ratio signals from wells containing cells using the respective blanks.
Wash cells with PBS on the day of the experiment.
Trypsinize cells using ∼3 ml trypsin solution in a humidified 37°C incubator for 2-4 min.
Suspend floating cells in 10 ml medium to stop trypsinization.
Transfer suspension to a 30-ml multipurpose container.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 10 min (3,000 rpm in Sorvall RT6000B).
Remove supernatant and wash cells with 10 ml cell wash buffer.
Centrifuge again at 200 × g for 10 min.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cells in 5 ml cell wash buffer.
Determine cell density using a Bürker-Türk counting chamber or any other method of choice.
Dispense increasing cell numbers into the wells of a black 96-well cell culture plate with clear bottom.
Adjust the volume of each well to 40 µl using cell wash buffer, including blank wells containing only 40 µl cell wash buffer without cells.
Add 35 µl cell assay solution to all wells.
Add 5 µl of 850 µM digitonin stock solution to all wells (final 50 µM).
Incubate for 10 min for full permeabilization of all cells.
Measure CFP and FRET signals of GEPII 1.0 over time using the CLARIOstar Plus fluorescence plate reader with excitation at 430-20 nm and emissions at 475-10 nm and 525-10 nm.
Use dichroic filters set to 455 and 480 nm with a gain of 2,000 for both emissions.
Adjust focal height to match the blank before measurement.
Calculate the FRET ratio signal by determining the FRET/CFP fluorescence (525 nm/475 nm) for all wells including blanks.
Perform blank correction on FRET ratio signals from wells containing cells using respective blanks.
If multiple blanks were used, calculate the average blank value and subtract it from each well of the respective condition.
Analyze and present the FRET ratio signal of GEPII 1.0.
Fit values using a proper regression to create the equation of the curve.
Solve for x as demonstrated in figure guidelines.
